description: Inputs of planner/flows captured from saved runs of public code; no model answer is stored and no expected label is written. The held-back cases follow the fixed rule of the lab (docs/runbooks/prompt-lab.md section 4).

flowCards.title: Open the catalog screen
flowCards.summary: The catalog form loads the discount, items, filters and shipment list when it opens.
flowCards.trigger: The application starts and the program's Main creates the view and controller and calls LoadView.
flowCards.outcome: The grid, brand and type filters, discount banner and shipment list are filled.

steps.text: Main creates the catalog view and a service client, wires them into the controller, and calls LoadView before showing the dialog.
The controller clears the grid, loads all items with the discount, and fills the grid with discounted prices.

flowCards.title: Record a stock shipment
flowCards.summary: A user adds stock for an item on a date and the stock record is saved.
flowCards.trigger: The user presses the Add Shipment button with an item, quantity and date filled in.
flowCards.outcome: The stock record is saved or updated and the form is cleared.

steps.text: The view checks that the item, quantity and date are present, and returns without action otherwise.
The view parses the values and raises the availability event for the controller.
The controller passes the shipment to the service, which overwrites or inserts the stock record.
The view shows the confirmation message and clears the inputs.

flowCards.title: Start the WinForms catalog application
flowCards.summary: The WinForms program creates the catalog view, a WCF client and the controller, then loads the screen.
flowCards.trigger: The WinForms executable starts.
flowCards.outcome: The catalog form is shown with its data loaded from the catalog service.

steps.text: Main creates the CatalogView, a CatalogServiceClient as the ICatalogService, and the CatalogController that joins them.
Main calls LoadView on the controller and then shows the form as a dialog.

flowCards.title: Open the catalog screen
flowCards.summary: The controller loads the discount banner, the catalog grid, the filters and the shipment list from the catalog service.
flowCards.trigger: The controller's LoadView is called at start-up.
flowCards.outcome: The form shows the discount banner, the catalog items with discounted prices, the brand and type filters and the shipment entry list.

steps.text: LoadView sets the controller on the view, then runs the discount check, the catalog load, the brand filter load, the type filter load and the shipment view load.
CheckForDiscounts asks the service for the discount valid today and, if one exists, sets the banner to a text giving the percentage and the end date.
LoadCatalogItems clears the grid, fetches the items for the brand and type filter, takes today's discount size and passes both to the view.
The view adds one grid row per item with its thumbnail, id, name, description and discounted price.
LoadBrandFilters and LoadTypeFilters fetch all brands and types and bind them to the combo boxes, each with an All entry of key 0.
SetShipmentView loads all items and fills the shipment list and the product id input.

flowCards.title: Add stock received for an item
flowCards.summary: A user records a quantity for an item on a date; the service overwrites an existing stock row for that item and date or inserts a new one.
flowCards.trigger: The user presses the add availability button on the catalog form.
flowCards.outcome: A stock row for the item and date holds the entered quantity, and the form shows a confirmation and clears its inputs.

steps.text: The button handler reads the selected item id, the quantity and the arrival date.
The controller builds a CatalogItemsStock and calls CreateAvailableStock on the service.
The service looks for an existing stock row with the same item and date; if one exists it sets its quantity and saves, otherwise it assigns the next StockId and inserts a new row.
The view then shows the message that the shipment was added and clears the product, quantity and date inputs.

components.name: Catalog web UI
components.responsibility: Razor Pages screens for browsing, creating, editing, viewing and deleting catalog items, and for the picture upload.

components.name: Catalog service
components.responsibility: Business rules for catalog items: paging, validation, id generation, stock updates and discount lookup.

components.name: Image service
components.responsibility: Stores temporary and final catalog pictures and builds picture URLs.

components.name: Catalog data access
components.responsibility: Entity Framework Core context for catalog items, brands, types, stock and discounts, with the hi-lo id generator.

components.name: Catalog seeder
components.responsibility: Creates the database on first run and seeds built-in or CSV catalog data.

flowCards.title: Browser request to the default MVC route
flowCards.summary: A browser request is handled by the web host, static files or MVC, and the default route.
flowCards.trigger: A browser sends an HTTP request to the site.
flowCards.outcome: The request is served as a static file, or dispatched to an MVC controller action, or to the error page on failure.

steps.text: The web host created in Program runs the Startup pipeline.
Static file requests are answered first by the static files middleware.
Other requests are matched by the default route and sent to a controller action, Catalog Index when no route values are given.

flowCards.title: Create a catalog item
flowCards.summary: A user submits the create form and the item is saved or the form is shown again with errors.
flowCards.trigger: The user submits the Create catalog item form (POST Catalog/Create).
flowCards.outcome: The item is created and the user sees the catalog index, or the form is shown again with its drop-downs filled.

steps.text: The POST checks the anti-forgery token and binds the submitted fields to a CatalogItem.
The controller checks the model state and, when valid, passes the item to the catalog service to create it.
After a successful create the user is redirected to the catalog index.

flowCards.title: Request a catalog item picture
flowCards.summary: A browser asks for the picture of a catalog item and receives the image bytes or an error status.
flowCards.trigger: An HTTP GET for items/{catalogItemId}/pic arrives.
flowCards.outcome: The image bytes are returned with a MIME type, or a 400 or 404 response is returned.

steps.text: The action rejects an id of zero or less with a 400 status.
The action loads the catalog item and builds the file path from an empty web root and the item's stored picture file name.
The MIME type is chosen from the file extension and the file bytes are read from disk and returned.

flowCards.title: Add a catalog item
flowCards.summary: A user opens the catalog list, goes to the create form, fills it in and submits it.
flowCards.trigger: The user presses Create New on the catalog index page.
flowCards.outcome: The form is posted with the entered values; the handler that saves the item is outside this area.

steps.text: The catalog index page shows the Create New link that goes to the Create action.
The create page shows the form with the brand and type drop-downs and the stock and price inputs.
The user presses Create to post the form, or Cancel to return to the Index action without posting.

flowCards.title: Application start-up and container wiring
flowCards.summary: When the web application starts, it builds the dependency container, registers the MVC and Web API configuration and sets up the database initializer unless mock data is used.
flowCards.trigger: The ASP.NET application starts (Application_Start in Global.asax.cs).
flowCards.outcome: MVC, Web API, areas, filters, routes and bundles are registered, and the catalog database initializer is set when mock data is off.

steps.text: Application_Start builds the Autofac container through RegisterContainer.
RegisterContainer registers the MVC and Web API controllers from this assembly and reads the UseMockData app setting to register ApplicationModule.
The container is set as the resolver for both MVC and Web API.
Application_Start then registers the Web API config, all areas, the global filters, the routes and the bundles.
ConfigDataBase sets the CatalogDBContext initializer to CatalogDBInitializer only when UseMockData is false.

components.name: Catalog web pages
components.responsibility: Razor Pages and MVC views for browsing, creating, editing, deleting and viewing catalog items and pictures.

components.name: Catalog service
components.responsibility: Applies catalog rules: paging, item lookup, create, update and delete, price and stock limits, and id assignment.

components.name: Catalog data access
components.responsibility: Reads and writes brands, types, items and stock in SQL Server through Entity Framework Core and the HiLo sequences.

flowCards.title: Delete a catalog item
flowCards.summary: A user confirms the removal of a catalog item from a delete page; the item is removed and the user returns to the index.
flowCards.trigger: The user opens the delete page for a catalog item and submits the confirmation form.
flowCards.outcome: The item is removed through the catalog service and the user is redirected to the catalog index.

steps.text: The delete page (GET) returns BadRequest without an id, loads the item by id and returns NotFound when none exists, then shows the item.
The confirmed POST (action name Delete) requires an anti-forgery token, loads the item by id and passes it to RemoveCatalogItem, then redirects to Index.

flowCards.title: Save a new catalog item
flowCards.summary: A posted new item is saved and the user returns to the catalog list, or the form is shown again with errors.
flowCards.trigger: The user submits the Create catalog item form (POST Catalog/Create).
flowCards.outcome: The item is created and the user is redirected to the catalog list, or the form is shown again with its validation errors.

steps.text: The POST action checks the anti-forgery token and binds only the listed catalog item fields.
The action passes the item to the catalog service to create it and redirects to the Index action.

flowCards.title: Show a page of the product catalogue
flowCards.summary: A visitor opens the home page and sees one page of products with pager links.
flowCards.trigger: The visitor requests Default.aspx, optionally with size and index route values.
flowCards.outcome: The product list shows one page of catalogue items and the pager links point to the previous and next pages.

steps.text: The page checks whether the route carries both size and index values.
The page asks the catalogue service for one page of items and logs the request.
The page binds the returned items to the product list and the list renders them.
The page sets the Previous and Next links to the ProductsByPageRoute with the neighbouring index, and hides Previous on the first page and Next on the last page.

flowCards.title: Create a catalog item
flowCards.summary: A user fills in the create form and submits it; a valid item is saved and the user is sent to the home page.
flowCards.trigger: The user presses the Create button on the Create catalog item page.
flowCards.outcome: A new catalog item is created through the catalog service and the browser is redirected to the home page.

steps.text: The page load writes a log entry and the page does nothing else on load.
Create_Click runs only when the page model state is valid; it builds a CatalogItem from the form fields, parsing Brand and Type ids as integers, Price as a decimal and the stock values as integers.
The item is passed to CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem.
The browser is redirected to the root URL (~).

flowCards.title: Edit a catalog item
flowCards.summary: The edit form is pre-filled on first load; a valid save updates the item and returns to the home page.
flowCards.trigger: The user opens the edit page for an item, then presses Save.
flowCards.outcome: The item is updated through the catalog service and the browser is redirected to the home page.

steps.text: On the first load, not on a postback, the page reads the item id from the route, loads the item and fills the Brand and Type dropdowns.
The item is passed to CatalogService.UpdateCatalogItem and the browser is redirected to the root URL (~).

components.name: Catalog web layer
components.responsibility: Serves the catalog pages and forms and handles the anti-forgery and sign-in checks on writes.

components.name: Catalog business service
components.responsibility: Lists, finds, creates, updates and deletes catalog items, checks item rules and pages results.

components.name: Catalog data access
components.responsibility: Reads and writes brands, types, items and stock in SQL Server through Entity Framework Core and issues hi-lo ids.

components.name: Picture service
components.responsibility: Serves and stores catalog item pictures and validates uploaded images.

flowCards.title: Host start-up and request pipeline
flowCards.summary: The web host builds the service container, then routes each HTTP request to a controller action by the default MVC route.
flowCards.trigger: The application starts, and afterwards each HTTP request reaches the host.
flowCards.outcome: The request is served by an MVC controller action, or by the error page in a non-development environment.

steps.text: Main builds the default web host with Startup as its startup class and runs it.
ConfigureServices registers MVC, reads the UseMockData setting, and when it is false registers the CatalogDBContext against the DefaultConnection string on SQL Server.
ConfigureServices builds an Autofac container, populates it from the service collection, registers ApplicationModule with the UseMockData flag, and returns it as the service provider.
Configure shows the developer exception page in development, otherwise it routes errors to /Home/Error, and it enables static files.
The MVC default route maps a URL of the form controller/action/id to the Catalog controller and Index action when no controller or action is given.

flowCards.title: Delete a catalog item
flowCards.summary: An editor confirms the deletion of a catalog item and the list is shown again.
flowCards.trigger: A POST to Catalog/Delete with an item id, sent from the delete confirmation page.
flowCards.outcome: The item has been passed to the service for removal and the user is redirected to the catalog list.

steps.text: The Delete GET action first checks the id and loads the item, showing it for confirmation.
DeleteConfirmed loads the item by id through the service and passes it to RemoveCatalogItem without checking for null.
The action redirects to Index.

components.name: Catalogue web layer
components.responsibility: Razor Pages and minimal API endpoints for the catalogue list, details, create, edit, delete, brands and pictures.

components.name: Catalogue business layer
components.responsibility: Catalogue rules: paging, item validation, picture URI, brand delete no-op and the rule that deletes do not cascade.

components.name: Catalogue data layer
components.responsibility: EF Core context and SQL Server 2022 catalogue tables with the seed data.

flowCards.title: Handling an incoming web request
flowCards.summary: The web host starts the application with Startup, then each HTTP request goes through the static-file step and the MVC default route, which points at the Catalog controller.
flowCards.trigger: An HTTP request arrives at the web host started by Program.Main.
flowCards.outcome: The request is served by a static file or routed to an MVC controller action, and unhandled errors go to the error page in non-development environments.

steps.text: Program.Main builds a default web host with Startup as its startup class and runs it.
The runtime calls ConfigureServices, which registers MVC and, when mock data is off, a CatalogDBContext on SQL Server, then builds an Autofac container with the ApplicationModule.
The runtime calls Configure, which enables the developer exception page in development, or the /Home/Error exception handler otherwise.
Static files are served before MVC routing.
MVC maps the default route {controller=Catalog}/{action=Index}/{id?}, so a request with no path reaches the Catalog controller's Index action.

flowCards.title: Create a catalog item
flowCards.summary: An administrator opens the create form, submits it, and the item is saved and the index is shown.
flowCards.trigger: The user opens Catalog/Create and then submits the form.
flowCards.outcome: The new item is saved and the user is redirected to the catalog index, or the form is shown again with errors.

steps.text: The GET action loads brand and type drop-down lists from the catalog service and shows an empty form.
The POST action checks the anti-forgery token and binds the form fields to a CatalogItem.
A valid item is passed to the catalog service's CreateCatalogItem, then the user is redirected to Index.

flowCards.title: Show a catalog picture
flowCards.summary: A browser requests a picture for a catalog item and gets the image file or an error.
flowCards.trigger: A request arrives at items/{catalogItemId}/pic.
flowCards.outcome: The image bytes are returned with the matching MIME type, or the request ends with a 400 or 404 response.

steps.text: The action rejects ids of zero or less with a 400 Bad Request.
The catalog service looks up the item by id.
The file path is built from an empty web root and the item's PictureFileName, the MIME type is picked from the extension, and the file bytes are returned.

components.name: Catalog web front end
components.responsibility: Serves the catalog list, details, create, edit, delete confirmation and picture pages to back-office users.

components.name: Catalog business service
components.responsibility: Applies catalog item rules such as paging, lookups, validation ranges and create, update and delete.

components.name: Catalog data access
components.responsibility: Reads and writes catalog items, brands and types in the SQL Server catalog database through Entity Framework Core.
